summary: Round 2 of T3-02, reviewed by Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). Reviewed commit 14af29a against base 4573b46. All six criteria pass. The round 1 fixes hold: round-trip tolerances are now asserted in plain metres, and the one rebuttal is justified. Both story checks pass. I did not independently re-verify the failing-first record or the mpmath reference arithmetic.

checks.criterion: Tests written and failing before implementation (recorded in notes)
checks.evidence: Author's record, not independently verified. The round 1 resolutions cite a failing run of 22 failed and 473 passed (2c6e7b9), and the test commits come before the fixes.

checks.criterion: Grid test: hand-computed corner and centre values for W=5000, D=90
checks.evidence: test_grid_matches_hand_computed_centres_for_5000_by_90 (test_geometry_aeqd.py:227) passes in the 498-test run. geometry.py:113-119 implements x_i and y_j as specified, with row 0 at the top.

checks.criterion: Inverse AEQD exact at rho=0 and at poles; independent forward round-trips at rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 in metres, for Moon, Mars and Earth at -89.9, -45, 0, 45 and 89.9 degrees
checks.evidence: 498 passed. The shared helper (test_geometry_aeqd.py:191-193) asserts RTOL and ATOL directly on metre coordinates, with no division by W. The at-centre return is explicit at geometry.py:226-229. The pole-centred tests have no NaN.

checks.criterion: Distance test: great-circle distance from the centre equals rho to 1e-9 relative, for all three radii
checks.evidence: test_great_circle_distance_from_the_centre_equals_rho (test_geometry_aeqd.py:510-517) asserts DISTANCE_RTOL with atol=0 and passes.

checks.criterion: Hypothesis property test of the round trip, with the longitude range stated
checks.evidence: test_round_trip_property (test_geometry_aeqd.py:556-569, 400 examples) passes. The longitude range is stated as [-pi, pi) in LONGITUDE_RANGE_RAD (geometry.py:127) and in the test_longitudes_are_normalised_to_minus_pi_inclusive_pi_exclusive test name. Continuous offsets within about 14 m of the centre are not checked at atol 1e-12 m; the property test uses D29 pixel centres, and the author documents the float64 limit.

checks.criterion: Terrain distances in metres live in geometry.py with no radar or model distance code
checks.evidence: geometry.py imports only math, dataclasses, types, typing and numpy. Two tests (test_geometry_imports_only_the_standard_library_and_numpy, test_importing_geometry_loads_no_other_terraluna_module) enforce this and pass.
Output showed ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed (9 files) and mypy found no issues. Exit status was not displayed, but no failure output appeared.
Changed files are pipeline/pyproject.toml, geometry.py, test_geometry_aeqd.py and uv.lock. All are on the story's file list. The diff stat is 1007 insertions.

findings.claim: The latitude is evaluated as phi0 + atan2(sin dphi, cos dphi), not the literal asin(S) the criterion names. The rebuttal is accepted.
findings.evidence: The docstring (:162-185) documents the deviation. test_inverse_matches_the_prd_expressions (:393-400) compares against the asin form at rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12. @terraluna/core (T10) must use the same evaluation for parity (PRD 8.8); the author flagged this as a human decision.

findings.claim: The 40-digit mpmath reference makes the independent-forward check stronger than the story required. It adds a dev dependency (pyproject.toml and uv.lock changed), and that dependency is in the story's files list.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat shows pipeline/pyproject.toml with +1 line and uv.lock changed. Both are in the story's files list.
